Found it: at step 2, keys has 2 elements but cnts has 1. That's the insert path:

```python
keys[idx] = seg[:p] + (key,) + seg[p:]
cnts[idx] = counts[:p] + (1,) + counts[p + 1:]
```
BUG! It should be `counts[p:]` not `counts[p+1:]` — when inserting a NEW key at position p, we splice in the new count without dropping anything. I mistakenly wrote `counts[p+1:]` (which was correct for the update-in-place case). Fix: `counts[:p] + (1,) + counts[p:]` ✓.

        assert c.count_lt(q) == sum(v for kk,v in ref.items() if kk<q), (step,q)
